title: Meat and fish
description: Name the meat and the fish, and say what is on the table.
grammar: gender and articles, and the plural of nouns
grammarNote: The words for meat are ordinary nouns, so they all need their article.

explanation.summary: Meat and fish are the food words a learner needs before a restaurant, and they follow the ordinary rules: a noun with a gender, an article, and a plural.

sections.heading: The nouns
sections.body: La carne is feminine and means meat in general. El pollo and el cerdo are masculine, and so is el pescado, which means fish as food. La ternera is the meat of a young cow, and la gamba is a prawn. Nothing here breaks the rule: -a is feminine, -o is masculine.

sections.heading: On the table
sections.body: In a shop you ask for what you want with un or una, and the noun tells you the gender: un piece of chicken is un pollo, and a piece of fish is un pescado. In the plural the article changes too: dos gambas is not dos gamba.

items.note: Masculine: el pescado. It means fish as food, not the animal.
Masculine: el salmón. The accent marks the stress.
